title: SSKR bridge version conflicts with the repository metadata policy
reproduction: Run pnpm check on the reviewed dirty tree. Root version is0.1.5; the canonical SSKR bridge and its Rust crate are0.1.6.
expected: The version policy, bridge metadata and generated runtime must agree before metadata/type/integrity checks can pass.
observed: pnpm check exits1 before tsc/no-copy execution: Project metadata is out of sync with package.json: packages/recovery-sskr-wasm/package.json, packages/recovery-sskr-wasm/rust/Cargo.toml, packages/recovery-sskr-wasm/rust/Cargo.lock, THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md. Run pnpm metadata:sync.
impact: Routine pnpm check and release verification cannot complete. The suggested synchronizer would downgrade bridge metadata to0.1.5 without rebuilding the0.1.6 WASM; that is not an acceptable audit workaround. No incorrect cryptographic output was established by this metadata failure.
recommendedFix: Choose and encode one supported bridge/release version policy. Keep Rust/package/notices/runtime versions aligned, then regenerate canonical WASM when Rust build inputs change. Do not blindly rewrite the source version while retaining another compiled bridge version.
requiredVerification: pnpm metadata:check and pnpm check; inspect exported bridge_version against metadata; canonical WASM comparison at release.

title: Canonical WASM record does not identify the reviewed inputs and SSKR output
reproduction: Run node tooling/verify-wasm-producers.mjs and node docs/audits/AUD-028-harnesses/inputs.mjs. Compare actual createWasmIntegrityManifest() with the retained canonical manifest.
expected: All four current source hashes and committed generated files match the canonical build record.
observed: The mandatory integrity gate exits1. All four sourceSha256 values differ; SSKR glue, declarations and WASM also differ. The other three generated directories match the retained record.
impact: The reviewed Rust/build source cannot be presented as canonically corresponding to the committed WASM. This mismatch is rejected correctly; it is not evidence of secret theft or tampering. The audit did not rewrite the record or run a canonical rebuild.
recommendedFix: After source/version decisions are final and at the authorized release check, regenerate with the canonical container and retain the exact record and comparison. Preserve the failing baseline evidence.
requiredVerification: Canonical uncached source/output comparison and node tooling/verify-wasm-producers.mjs; review each changed generated file. No host-only manifest rewrite.

title: Default Dash Deriver build rejects the checked MnemoCode SSKR platform module
reproduction: Run pnpm build:html with default features, then the Dash Deriver artifact verifier. Compare a derive-only Dash composition.
expected: Both supported default editions compile with their intended modules; graph admission retains Dash-only protocol exclusion.
observed: Four multi-chain tools and Dash Viewer/Scanner compile; the default Dash Deriver fails: graph contains inputs outside the Dash allowlist: packages/recovery-backup/src/mnemocode-share-platform.ts (reported twice because of separate graphs). Independently built Dash Inspector and derive-only Dash Deriver compile. The old default Dash Deriver fails the current source fingerprint verifier.
impact: The default Dash package cannot be built from current source. An old local page remains; a branding-only pass does not prove source freshness. The new platform gate is protocol-neutral; no excluded coin behavior was demonstrated.
recommendedFix: Review and admit this specific protocol-neutral module in the Dash graph owner; retain exclusions for actual non-Dash implementations. Add a default-MnemoCode composition regression.
requiredVerification: Both default builds and current artifact verifiers; Dash branding/exclusion gate; minimal derive-only and MnemoCode+SSKR selective combinations.

title: Candidate-list admission buffers an oversized file before rejecting it
reproduction: Use the real importer and panel Select/Open actions with synthetic oversized File metadata and an arrayBuffer spy returning only a small invalid header. No large allocation is needed.
expected: Read only a bounded header and reject unsupported file sizes before whole-file buffering.
observed: All three entry points call arrayBuffer once before rejection. The subsequent 64 KiB header restriction cannot bound this initial allocation.
impact: A locally selected untrusted large file can consume excessive memory before format rejection. Host exhaustion was not attempted; no remote trigger or secret egress was shown. The importer accepts an arrayBuffer-only interface, so the primary admission fix belongs to the actual file selection/Open owner and its format limits.
recommendedFix: Read a bounded header slice, derive one format-owned encrypted/plaintext size ceiling, and enforce it before and during buffering/decryption.
requiredVerification: Oversized metadata refuses without arrayBuffer; valid small files and boundary-size headers still import; streaming/body size is bounded.

title: Early Orchard preparation errors bypass owned-secret cleanup
reproduction: Capture the decoder-owned synthetic viewing-key buffer and fail each note field width; separately have shielded derivation throw after capturing its wrapper-owned seed copy.
expected: Owned secret allocations enter a wiping scope immediately; caller-owned inputs remain unchanged.
observed: Four note preparation failures retain decoded key bytes. A throwing derivation retains the copied seed. In-scope engine/guard failures wipe correctly, and the supplied caller seed stays unchanged. The viewing buffer retained95nonzero bytes out of96; the seed copy retained64outof64.
impact: Avoidable secret memory residue on exceptional paths, not demonstrated exfiltration or extraction. Provider admission limits ordinary malformed-note reachability in Discovery; arbitrary library inputs and injected failures establish ownership gaps. The harness retained references to observe missing explicit wiping; it cannot establish post-GC persistence or real trap frequency.
recommendedFix: Move fallible preparation into the owning try/finally immediately after allocation; safely dispose partially initialized buffers.
requiredVerification: Each preparation, derivation and registration failure wipes owned copies; successful results and caller ownership remain correct.

title: Read-only SDK gate misses known writes behind transparent TypeScript expressions
reproduction: Analyze declare const sdk:any plus (sdk as any).addresses.transfer({}), (<any>sdk).addresses.transfer({}) and (sdk satisfies any).addresses.transfer({}). Do not execute those calls.
expected: The same known write method is detected regardless of a transparent type expression.
observed: The direct-call control is detected once and a read-only control passes; all three assertion variants yield zero detections.
impact: An inadvertent known write call can evade the source integrity check. No active first-party production write call was found; the experiment is static analysis, not a broadcast.
recommendedFix: Unwrap AsExpression, TypeAssertion and SatisfiesExpression alongside parentheses/non-null expressions; retain alias/computed-call handling.
requiredVerification: Direct, alias, assertion, optional and computed known write fixtures fail the gate; read-only fixtures still pass.

title: Address descriptors reject valid Bech32m Taproot addresses
reproduction: Render the literal BIP86 P2TR script, then compile its checksummed addr(bc1p5cyxnuxmeuwuvkwfem96lqzszd02n6xdcjrs20cac6yqjjwudpxqkedrcr) descriptor through decodeDescriptor.
expected: Recover the exact published script and address, while rejecting corrupted checksums, wrong networks and v1 encoded with Bech32.
observed: The independent script-to-address control passes. addr() fails with Invalid checksum in the valid Bech32m address because bech32.decode is called before selecting the checksum family. Negative controls pass.
impact: A supported Taproot address descriptor cannot be inspected. No incorrectly generated address was demonstrated.
recommendedFix: Use the shared witness-address decoder, then enforce witness version, checksum family and selected network in one owner.
requiredVerification: Literal v0/v1 address descriptors, Base58 controls, both networks/regtest and wrong checksum-family refusals.

title: Unknown Dash PSBT fields acquire unsupported Bitcoin verification semantics
reproduction: Parse a supported Dash v0 one-input/one-output PSBT, adding unknown input keys0x11 and0x13 with empty values. Compare semantic checks and signing analysis to the unmodified control.
expected: Preserve unknown bytes without deriving Bitcoin locktime or signature conclusions from them.
observed: Each unknown field changes Dash semantic conclusions although the chain-aware schema skips its validation. Bitcoin controls reject the same malformed known fields.
impact: Unvalidated unknown data receives verification/signing labels. This is not signature verification or demonstrated spending capability.
recommendedFix: Use the chain-aware field registry throughout relationship, locktime and signing analysis, not only structural admission.
requiredVerification: Adding each Dash unknown field preserves known semantic conclusions and raw bytes; valid Bitcoin known fields keep their intended behavior.

title: Dash previous-transaction parser accepts malformed special-payload framing
reproduction: Feed special Dash wire transactions with a truncated payload, nonminimal CompactSize payload length and an extra trailing byte to readTransaction and the actual PSBT non-witness UTXO path.
expected: Validate the wire payload length, canonical prefix and complete consumption separately from any PSBT-global representation.
observed: All six malformed direct/PSBT-path cases are accepted. Valid length-prefixed transaction and txid/outpoint binding controls pass.
impact: Malformed previous transactions pass structural inspection. No consensus acceptance, valid blockchain inclusion or unauthorized spending was established.
recommendedFix: Introduce explicit wire framing for previous transactions and retain the documented global-PSBT payload representation separately.
requiredVerification: Pinned Dash special-transaction positives plus truncated/nonminimal/trailing negatives through direct and PSBT entry points.

title: Platform address history is relabeled without checking its resource identity
reproduction: Use the actual history lookup with three small mocked HTTP replies; change info.bech32mAddress to another valid resource while keeping its supported schema/network.
expected: Reject a response for a different resource before using totals/history.
observed: The lookup resolves and labels returned indexed history with the requested address. Matching-resource control passes and wrong-network control rejects.
impact: Auxiliary indexed history can be shown under an unrelated proof-verified address. The address-balance proof does not authenticate this auxiliary response.
recommendedFix: Share the resource/network normalization and binding checks already enforced by Discovery; distinguish proof-backed state from indexed history.
requiredVerification: Missing/mismatched resource rejects; equivalent normalized resource succeeds; proof state and auxiliary history remain separately labeled.

title: Core CSV exports label a pending transaction as confirmed
reproduction: Serialize a supported pending Core transaction with null block/time, zero confirmations and both lock flags false through createViewerExport.
expected: Use pending/unconfirmed confirmation status; retain lock information separately.
observed: Parsed CSV row status is confirmed, while the confirmed control also serializes successfully.
impact: Consumers receive an incorrect confirmation label. No provider query or wallet mutation was performed.
recommendedFix: Derive confirmation state from authoritative block/confirmation fields rather than the absence of lock flags.
requiredVerification: Inspect actual single/batch CSV for pending, confirmed and locked combinations with null/zero distinction.

title: Core JSON and CSV invent a confirmed/unconfirmed balance split
reproduction: Export reported balance5, received10, sent7 and derived discrepancy2 through actual JSON and CSV serializers.
expected: Preserve the reported balance and discrepancy without assigning undocumented confirmation semantics.
observed: JSON uses confirmedDuffs=5 and unconfirmedDuffs=2; CSV metadata uses unconfirmed_duffs=2. The normalizer explicitly treats this as an undocumented derived discrepancy.
impact: Consumers may misclassify amounts or double-count the derived difference. The raw reported balance itself is preserved.
recommendedFix: Publish neutral reported-balance/discrepancy fields and document the export schema migration; keep all formats aligned.
requiredVerification: Literal parsed JSON/CSV/XLSX fields for positive, negative and zero discrepancy; no unsupported confirmation claims.

title: Incomplete Orchard CSV marks provisional unspent notes as spendable
reproduction: Export a synthetic incomplete FVK ledger snapshot with one recovered incoming note whose provisional spent flag is false.
expected: An incomplete spend scan reports unknown for provisional unspent notes; observed spends remain known.
observed: The summary says partial but the note CSV row says spendable. Complete-FVK, IVK-unknown and observed-spent partial controls pass.
impact: A spend outside the scanned prefix may be overlooked by CSV consumers. No current-chain balance or spending authority was established.
recommendedFix: Require complete FVK coverage before labeling unspent notes spendable; reuse the completeness-aware presentation contract.
requiredVerification: Actual serialized complete/partial FVK, IVK/OVK and known-spent cases remain consistent with summaries and other formats.

title: NaN concurrency silently resolves local searches without executing jobs
reproduction: Call both actual search entry points with one synthetic target, a counting lookup callback and concurrency:Number.NaN; compare concurrency1 controls.
expected: Reject or deliberately normalize invalid concurrency without skipping supplied jobs.
observed: Both NaN calls resolve with resultLength1, populatedSlots0 and lookupCalls0. Both concurrency1 controls execute the supplied job.
impact: An API caller can receive a sparse apparently successful result without a search. Production UI reachability was not established.
recommendedFix: Use one finite safe-integer concurrency validator and bounded scheduler, retaining seed cleanup in the seed-owning layer.
requiredVerification: NaN/Infinity/fractional/negative/zero and bounds follow an explicit safe policy; every accepted job executes with complete result slots, ordering and cancellation preserved.

title: Module-boundary import extraction ignores dynamic imports
reproduction: Read and execute the exact private gate extractor in isolation on equivalent static and valid dynamic cross-application import syntax; do not import the foreign application.
expected: Both forms contribute the same resolved dependency edge.
observed: The static control resolves apps/activity-viewer/src/app.js; dynamic import yields an empty edge list because the regex requires whitespace after import.
impact: Boundary/cycle tests omit a supported module edge form. No current forbidden production edge was established; build graph checks are separate mitigation.
recommendedFix: Resolve static imports, re-exports and dynamic imports through the TypeScript parser/module resolver rather than a whitespace regex.
requiredVerification: Static/dynamic/aliased cross-app and package-cycle fixtures are detected; valid dynamic Dash runtime imports remain permitted.

title: Derivation path previews and runtime paths have separate policy owners
reproduction: Compare the adapter metadata path builders with each runtime derivation path builder for the same protocol, network, account and branch.
expected: One crypto-free protocol profile owns the segment order, hardening and rendering consumed by both metadata and runtime.
observed: Bitcoin, Dash and Ethereum reconstruct the same path rules independently. No currently incorrect path was established in the reviewed samples.
impact: A path-policy change can update display and derivation differently. This is a concrete DRY/ownership violation with maintainability impact, not demonstrated key loss.
recommendedFix: Extend crypto-free protocol profiles with path methods and make both metadata and runtime delegate to them.
requiredVerification: Compare metadata preview paths and actual requested derivation paths at account/branch boundaries for each adapter; retain independent output vectors.

title: CoinJoin protocol identity remapping is repeated in UI and protocol modules
reproduction: Trace dash-core-coinjoin resolution through the matcher scope/UI and runtime protocol adapter metadata.
expected: The crypto-free protocol metadata owner resolves runtime identity and display name.
observed: Three consumers special-case dash-core-coinjoin to dash-core; the UI also synthesizes the protocol label.
impact: A protocol mapping change requires synchronized edits in independent consumers. No wrong current CoinJoin address was demonstrated.
recommendedFix: Expose a metadata resolver owned by the protocol profile; keep the page independent of cryptographic runtime imports.
requiredVerification: Matcher scopes, preview labels and runtime registry resolve CoinJoin consistently in both editions.
